::: {.entry-meta}
[new component]{.chip .built} Entry 18 · milestone M3
:::

M2 closed on 3 October with its three acceptance criteria met ([M2 page](../milestones/M2.qmd));
active learning moved into M3 ([OQ-18](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-18)). M3 trains the surrogates: neural networks that return
TGLF's turbulent fluxes from TGLF's local inputs, fast enough to call at every radius and time
step (see the [Primer](../primer.qmd)). The owner set one ensemble per machine, every TGLF case
kept, and the fluxes learned in a signed-log space, $\mathrm{sign}(Q)\ln(1+|Q|)$ with $Q$ in
gyro-Bohm units (gB), because the heat fluxes in the datasets span many orders of magnitude
([K-019](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-019)). The accuracy target was to be set after a first baseline.

## Two networks

The baseline is a deep ensemble of 10 multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), each with four hidden
layers of 256 units, trained on the same cases and differing in initialisation and minibatch
order. The members' mean is the prediction; their spread is the uncertainty.

The owner then asked for a recreation of TGLF-NN, the neural-network version of TGLF developed
at General Atomics (GA) and distributed in TurbulentTransport.jl under Apache-2.0 (Neiser et
al., APS-DPP 2022). GA's training procedure is not published; the model files are, and we read
the architecture from them. Each of 20 members is a residual network of width 32: an input
layer, five blocks of four dense layers with a skip connection around each block, and a linear
output layer. It takes GA's choice of inputs, including the pressure and q gradients, and
standardises its outputs linearly. We train it with our loss, optimiser and data. GA's trained
weights are not used.

## Held-out errors and learning curves

Each machine's 10^5^ cases are split at random into training, validation and test sets
(80/10/10). The test cases are used once, at the end; the error is that of the ensemble mean
against TGLF, on cases with |Q| above 1 gB.

| network | outputs | median relative error of Q~e~ and Q~i~ |
|---|---|---|
| MLP ensemble | signed-log | [MAST-U 0.77 (Q_e) and 0.80 (Q_i); ITER 0.61 and 0.62]{.claim}[C-077](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-077){.cid .st-measured} |
| TGLF-NN, as distributed | linear, standardised | [MAST-U 9.1 (Q_e) and 17.7 (Q_i); ITER 6.8 and 7.0; R² of Q_e in signed-log space -0.30 (MAST-U) and -0.35 (ITER)]{.claim}[C-078](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-078){.cid .st-measured} |
| TGLF-NN | signed-log | [MAST-U 0.75 (Q_e) and 0.77 (Q_i); ITER 0.60 and 0.58]{.claim}[C-079](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-079){.cid .st-measured} |

GA's linear output scaling fails on these datasets. Standardising divides each flux by its
standard deviation over the training set, and the high-flux tail sets that value:
[2.5 × 10^5^ gB (MAST-U) and 1.1 × 10^4^ gB (ITER); the median |Q_e|, 473 and 29 gB, is 0.0019 and 0.0027 standard deviations]{.claim}[C-085](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-085){.cid .st-measured}. A squared-error loss in those units is decided by the largest cases, and
the typical case is not learned. GA's training fluxes come from measured profiles and stay in
a bounded range ([GA's MAST-U model -1.5 × 10^4^ to 5.2 × 10^4^ gB; tglf-mastu-v1 -2.4 × 10^6^ to 2.8 × 10^7^ gB]{.claim}[C-086](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-086){.cid .st-measured}), where the same scaling works. On signed-log targets the
same network matches the MLP ensemble with about a tenth of the parameters per member
([21 827 per member (TGLF-NN network) against 203 526 (MLP)]{.claim}[C-080](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-080){.cid .st-measured}), and its spread covers the TGLF value more often ([TGLF-NN network 0.63 (MAST-U) and 0.66 (ITER); MLP ensemble 0.54 and 0.57]{.claim}[C-081](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-081){.cid .st-measured}).
Neither spread is calibrated; calibration is part of M4.

Retraining on a quarter and on half of the training split gives learning curves that are still
falling at 80000 cases, with slopes [-0.10 (MAST-U) and -0.19 (ITER) for the TGLF-NN network; -0.07 and -0.14 for the MLP]{.claim}[C-083](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-083){.cid .st-measured}. A median error of 0.30 would need, by
extrapolation, [about 3 × 10^6^ cases (ITER) and about 10^9^ (MAST-U)]{.claim}[C-084](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-084){.cid .st-preliminary} drawn as in the M2 datasets. Both networks give nearly the
same curves, so we suspect the sampling (a uniform box, mostly far above the instability
threshold) more than the network; that is not yet tested.

What checks these numbers: the test cases took no part in training or in choosing the
parameters each member keeps (that used the validation set). The blog's figure script
recomputes the medians from the saved models with its own code and reproduces the stored
values. The comparison with GA is not independent: the network, training code and metrics
are ours, and only the architecture is GA's.

M3 is in progress. The active-learning round that followed, and the accuracy target set
afterwards ([OQ-19](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-19)), are in [entry 19](19-active-learning-round-1.qmd).
